data.gender_notes: Paritosh is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Paritosh is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Paritosh', which means 'God's Gift'. It is a name of great significance in Hindu culture, often given to newborn boys to symbolize the divine blessings they receive. The name Paritosh carries the meaning “God's Gift” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Paritosh usually hope their child will grow to embody god's gift and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: Paritosh is a beautiful and poetic name in the Hindu tradition. In this rich cultural context, Paritosh carries an exalted and profound meaning. The name is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Paritosh', which signifies 'God's Gift' or 'An offering of God'. The name is a constant reminder of the divine grace that surrounds us and inspires a sense of reverence for the divine.
data.spiritual_significance: For Hindus, the name Paritosh holds deep spiritual significance. As the name suggests, it symbolizes the belief that every human being is a manifestation of God and that life is a divine gift bestowed upon us. The name inspires a sense of devotion, gratitude, and humility towards the divine and reminds us to cherish and honor this precious gift of life. It is a constant reminder of the immense spiritual potential and possibilities that lie within each one of us.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Paritosh, meaning 'supreme pleasure' or 'great joy', symbolizes the innate human quest for happiness and fulfillment, reminding us of the importance of finding joy in life's simple pleasures and cherishing the blessings bestowed upon us.

vedic_reference.note: Paritosh is derived from the Sanskrit word ‘paritoshana’, which means ‘desiring, wishing, longing’. It is not directly related to any Vedic or mythological reference.

historical_references.reference: Paritosh was a renowned scholar and the court poet of Emperor Harshavardhana, who ruled Kaushikaratna (Thanesar) in the 7th century AD. He is famous for his work 'Parasarabhava', a Sanskrit drama based on the life of Parasara, the father of Ved Vyas, the author of the Mahabharata and the Bhagavad Gita.
historical_references.context: Court poet and scholar under Emperor Harshavardhana

historical_references.reference: Paritosh is mentioned in the works of the 12th century Jain author Hemachandra, who wrote about Paritosh's Jain background and his significant contributions to Jain literature. One of his works, 'Parishatak', is a commentary on the Jain scripture 'Agama'.
